utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'll try and be very brief because yesterday I managed to study the documentation that was delivered to us by our learned friend yesterday, before the beginning of the cross-examination. So I would like to draw your attention to the thing that I have been drawing to your attention to all the time, and those are the documents which have major omissions in them, and that is why I consider them unusable. I shall start with documents -- it is interesting that all these documents show as their source the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina, so I would kindly ask the Prosecutor to tell us what he considers to be the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as we all know only too well that such a government does not exist. Let me draw your attention to the first document, P123 in English original, it has two pages. On page 2, some sentences have been added subsequently, Joker and Andric are the words added and they don't exist in the Croatian original, there is no page 2 and there are no additions. Interestingly enough that 8367, that numbers are in sequence, 8367 and 8368. So we are talking about Exhibit 5123, look at the second page of the English translation and look at the Croatian original. There is no second page, nor is it mentioned anywhere in the Croatian original. And the source is still the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Even more striking example is Exhibit P127. Please look at the English translation, where it says that it was signed and stamped, signed by General Major Ante Roso. There is no signature. The stamp in the Croatian original is illegible. One could maybe conclude that this is the Main Staff of Herceg-Bosna and that's the end of it. It is a totally illegible copy and somethings added by hand, namely the sentences. First in capital letters, and then somebody added by hand, in the Croatian original, all these things, which obviously you can't see in the English translation. Another confusing thing, same objections, may be addressed to Exhibit P339. I apologise, Your Honours, the Prosecutor changed it into P348, although you have already adopted the same exhibit under number P339, earlier on, so why has the number been changed and why has the exhibit being introduced under a new number? I don't know. You will come to an English text which says, "Command structure for the HV army." The Prosecutor's number has been crossed out and one person added by hand, I don't know, Your Honours whether you have it in front of you, somebody added by hand, "Signed by Alija Izetbegovic, signed by Mate Boban, signed by General Sefer Halilovic, signed by General Petkovic and also added by hand in Zagreb, 23 April, 1993.. We don't know the source of this document. There is no sign of the archives. Again what is mentioned is the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is really interesting that the text is there printed and then somebody adds, by hand, and as if these people were on the document originally. Further on, Your Honours, there is a transcript of an interview, given by Mr. Bender to the Croatian television. The name of the programme is "Picture in Pictures. "Slikom na Sliku.". The source for that again is the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina, although the -- this is Croatian Television, but we don't know the date when this show aired, the year when this show aired, why no data whatsoever about this document, and it is really surprising that again the source is the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Further on, Your Honours, document P239.2. Both the English original and the Croatian copy have not been signed, so they have not been signed by any one person. And since these are UN documents, at least that is what it says on the documents, I believe that these documents have to be signed in person, if they are signed. And finally, Your Honours, let me just find this document, Mr. Prosecutor has provided us with a copy of a joint -- the notorious joint statement that has been disputed here and the dispute is about whether it has been signed by misters Boban and Izetbegovic, a copy that he provided us with earlier on is very much different from the one that he provided us with yesterday. So we are talking about the joint statement issued on the 2nd of April, 1993. Your Honours, you can see that this copy is clean. However, the one that we received in the last binder on the top of the page it says, in the Ekavian dialect "Boban's proposal." That has been added by hand. And the source again is the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I apologise, Your Honours, here it says that is Exhibit P271, in capital letters you can see it, added by hand, "Boban's proposal." Whereas in the statement that we received earlier on, this does not exist. The Defence has every reason to doubt the sources of -- for these documents. It doubts that it is the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. We don't have to be experts on constitutional and legal matters, but still, we have to be certain that this has not been sent by any ministers. There -- the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina certainly did not exist in 1993. We would like to establish who is it who gives these documents to the OTP, the Defence claims that it has -- it is being done AID -- by AID. That's what I've always been saying, and I have always been right. I believe that this is a secret terrorist, political police, serving just one component, one party, and one army, and that is the Bosniak Muslim one. Secondly, Your Honours, I have the correspondence about our requests to the OTP, I'm not going to enumerate all the dates of these letters, and we, in these documents, asked for the disclosure of documents. Very soon you will hear the testimony -- I now have the reliable data that the Prosecutor, i.e. the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal, has received many documents of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as long ago as in 1995 and some they received in 1996. And especially in the past few years, those are the documents which are relative to item 5, and that is the general distribution, widespread, of the crimes allegedly committed by HVO after the 16th of April in the entire territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I claim that the Prosecutor has documents originating from the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina dating back before 16 of April, talking about their orders and their attacks on the HVO, which would mean -- which would be beneficial for us in respect of item 5. So I would kindly ask the Prosecutor to disclose these documents, and we would like to ask Their Honours to issue a binding order and we are going to ask for such orders for a number of institutions and some persons that we are going to call to testify. I am kindly asking you to start the closed session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, while the witness comes in, I've just listened to your ruling or your statements, and the Defence finds itself in a Catch-22. You stated that you believe all exculpatory evidence in possession of the Prosecution will be turned over to us. We are in a situation that we are being dictated what documents might be relevant to our defence by the Prosecution. We cannot point out what documents we want until we see them, and all we are asking is that we could have a time to sit down with the Prosecutor's investigator in their office and look through the documents, then we could advise ourselves or be convinced that in fact there are no exculpatory documents in regards to the army of BiH.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, I'm sorry to tell you that every Defence team before this Tribunal, facing the same problem with you. And there are jurisprudence before this Tribunal concerning the criteria of the exculpatory documents. The meetings between the two parties are encouraged by this Trial Chamber, but so far as I know, whether this document is exculpatory will be decided by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If that's your ruling for the record, then we know what it is. The other thing real quickly is on the Witness SS. I understand your seized with that motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if we are talking about this witness, shall we go back to the closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm not going to mention any other names. I'm going to ask you, we have seven days to file a response and we are getting ready to do that Your Honour, so I ask you not to make any rulings before you receive our response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So could we have the witness, please? [The witness entered court].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Will you please sit down? Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, as I'm sure the Court will understand, my remaining time will, of course, start now. And not the past half hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not sure I heard your testimony during direct examination correctly on this point or not, but if I did, you said something about the effect that the HDZ BiH, that is the political party by that name, froze its activities sometime in 1993 or 1994. Is that what you told us?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. The HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not work in 1993 and 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did it become active again after that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know exactly which month it was, but there part -- it was simply a moratorium on the activity of the party and after that period it resumed its normal functions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In fact, sir, isn't it true that that party has been extremely active for the past several years and is still active today, correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the foundation of the Croat Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina, let me not repeat it not to waste time, we were very active. We are active today because we take part in all the walks of life in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, are you currently seeking or being considered for the position of the President of the HDZ BiH for Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, your information is not correct. On the 11th of May, we elected acting president of the Croat Democratic Union, and that is Barisa Colak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, were you seeking prior to the 11th of May, sir, were you seeking or being considered for that position?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the election of the acting president, there were various considerations, various suggestions. My name figured in those because I'm also a member of the Presidency of the Croat Democratic Union.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that during 1993 time period, that for all practical purposes Franjo Tudjman made all the important decisions for the HDZ BiH?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Prosecutor. That is not so. Mr. Franjo Tudjman, the president of the Republic of Croatia and president of the HDZ of the Republic of Croatia, did not take any decisions on behalf of the Croat Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina. We, the members of the Croat Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina and relevant bodies adopted and prepared all the necessary decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir, so if on a review of these documents that are described as the presidential transcripts, we have I put it to you instance after instance of President Tudjman directing and making decisions for the HDZ delegations coming from Herceg-Bosna, you would deny that? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a fact that we attended some meetings at the president's -- president of the Republic of Croatia and the president of the HDZ of the Republic of Croatia, Mr. Tudjman, but it was at the time when the international community had made President Tudjman responsible and authorised him to represent, to a certain degree, the Croats or rather the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And we too decided to give him those powers, but in all the meetings where the future of the Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina was being discussed, there was also our delegation present, that is the delegation of the HDZ of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, during the time period from 1992 and continuing into 1995 and thereafter, didn't you frequently refer to President Franjo Tudjman of Croatia as quote "your president" or " our president"?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Franjo Tudjman is the President of the Republic of Croatia. He is the President of the HDZ of the Republic of Croatia, and it is a custom for, amongst us Croats to say often that President Tudjman is the President of all the Croats, but it has nothing to do with the state or any other system. I believe you know that Article, I believe, 10 of the constitution of the Republic of Croatia specifies that the Republic of Croatia takes care of the Croats outside the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And as part of his control over the HDZ BiH, sir, is it not correct that it was President Franjo Tudjman and his closest advisers in the government of Croatia who removed Mate Boban as the President of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna in late 1993 or early 1994?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I heard is not true. After an all-round analysis, competent bodies of the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna and the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna removed the president of the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina and president of the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it a fact that by late 1993, President Franjo Tudjman and the government of Croatia was under intense pressure from the international community because of the conduct of the Croatian community and subsequently Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, the conduct of the HDZ in Herceg-Bosna and the conduct of the HVO and as a result of that pressure, President Tudjman removed Mr. Boban, correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: President Boban was removed from his offices by us. I said members of the Croat Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and members of the House of Representatives of the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna. And I learned only from the press and other media that I could hear that the Republic of Croatia, that President Tudjman and the government of the Republic of Croatia were under certain pressure of the international community.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you've said throughout your testimony that you were one of the founders and senior leaders of the HDZ BiH, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna and in fact at one point, on the first day of your testimony, you said that you were part of, and I believe I quote a part of the transcript, "a small circle of the leadership." Sir, are you telling the Judges here that you are one of the people responsible for the policy and practices of the HDZ in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna toward the Muslims who were located in the territory of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that from the beginning, I was a member of the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna and one of its founders. And also one of the founders of the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna, and that I occupied the highest posts. I am also one of the founders of the Croat Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina and I participated in the work of the relevant institutions, in which we adopted our platforms our programmes and took the necessary decisions. And as for the Muslims, from our discussion, the previous one and the one that will follow, you will see that the Croat Democratic Union is indeed democratic, and that it never resorted to any methods that would not fall into that category. I wish to point out here one thing that I said at a number of meetings: If, in the course of the activities of certain relevant bodies, there perhaps were certain omissions or certain crimes, then I requested, and I requested here too, that those who did that or who possibly did that, need to be called to account before relevant institutions and suffer the consequences as prescribed by law.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to put my question to you again very specifically, whether you believe that the policies of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, whether you believe they were good or bad, whether you believe they were discriminatory or not discriminatory, are the Judges of this Chamber to understand that you are one of the persons responsible for those policies and practices?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The policy of the Croat Democratic Union, that is the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna and the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna did -- was not at variance with international democratic standards. It was public. It was not discriminatory, and all the peoples who lived in that area enjoyed an equal treatment. As for the legislative branch of the government, and especially after I was elected the President of the House of Representatives of the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna, sometime in early 1994, I was one of the most responsible persons for the conduct of the legislative branch of the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And this is the legislature that yesterday, under oath, you can't tell us how often they met or where they met or in fact if they met hardly at all, correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, that is not true, because yesterday, we did not discuss the work of the House of Representatives of the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna. We talked yesterday about the work of the Presidency of the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna in 1992 and part of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, turning to the documents, the HVO and HDZ documents, can you please -- you've indicated, I believe, in so many words, you have nothing to hide and Mr. Krsnik said he has nothing to hide. Can you tell us where these documents are located, please?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- all the archives of the institutions of the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna, the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna is duly archived, but every agency, every body kept its archive in a different place. Until I was removed from these legislative duties, this documentation was in Mostar and elsewhere. I believe it is still there, unless --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Give us the street address in Mostar so that all of us, to assist the Chamber, can please obtain these very important documents. Can you give me the street address in Mostar where the documents are located?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we go into private session, please, for a second?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in the open session. Witness, you may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The archive of the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna and the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna is the property of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Ask the relevant authorities through regular channels, and you will get all the necessary documentation. However, I need to point out that it is a fact that there have been cases, because I know that, when SFOR members broke into some archives and did what counsel Krsnik mentioned. Let me sum up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... my question I'm going to come back to it very specifically. Tell me, please, as far as you know, where they are located and if you say there are several, please pick one, pick one in Mostar, please give me the street address and tell me where this archive is located?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not been directly involved in all that for the past three years, and I do not know what went on during that time, but I repeat, use the regular procedure, ask for it from the federation agencies, the agencies of Bosnia-Herzegovina and I believe they know where that documentation is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When was the last time, sir, that you, yourself visited, actually visited and saw one of these archives?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The archive of the House of Representatives of the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna, whilst it still existed, that is until the Dayton Accords, and the transfer of powers from the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna to the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Bosnia and Herzegovina, these documents were kept on the premises of the House of Representatives of the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna, and the secretary of the House of Representatives, Mr. Mile Kudic, was responsible for the storage and proper keeping of the archive.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what was that location, sir? The physical location of those documents?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Physically, physically, it was in Mostar. I'm not sure what the street is called but you can check it very easily. I'm sure everybody knows it because streets change their names, so on the premises of the House of Representatives of the Assembly of the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna. And I believe I'm quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I repeat my question to you, sir. When was the last time you, Ivan Bender, saw one of these -- was physically present at any one of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. these archives?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that I was physically present every day whilst the House of Representatives functioned, and that was, I believe, late 1995. That is right up to the Dayton Accords, I had access to this documentation, because this is the documentation of the House of Representatives of the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna, which was subsequently placed under the jurisdiction of the parliament of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that is Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you've told?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Bender, I want to remind you that witnesses who come before this Tribunal are under an obligation to answer questions. You have come very close in my view to what would be considered contempt of this Court. I posed many questions to you which you failed to answer. Mr. Krsnik tried to get you to answer. And now Mr. Scott is asking you the same question. I want to remind you of your position here. You are under an obligation to answer questions that this Chamber deems are legitimately put to you. You have stated that you attended at the house of representatives almost every day until 1995 and yet you appear to be refusing to furnish this Court with the address of that place that you attended every day for years. We don't care if the name of the place has changed. What was the address of that place when you attended it every day? That's the first question. Secondly, Mr. Scott asked you twice when did you last actually physically see the archive? Not when you were last in the building where you believe it was kept. When did you last physically, actually see the archive? I'm sorry if I'm being strict with you, Mr. Bender. I think it's time that we were clear about your position vis-a-vis this Tribunal, your obligation to answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Clark, I think that yesterday there was a misunderstanding. I believe we talked at cross-purposes during questions and answers, because of our different political systems. The political system that you come from and the one that I come from. If you have time and if you allow me, we can talk about this further. As for the archive of the House of Representatives of the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna, I do not know about any other archive because other people are responsible for it, the street had no name at the time so it had the address as I said, "House of Representatives, Hrvatski Dom, of the Croat Republic in Mostar" so the street didn't have a name, no number. Later on the streets were given names but which is it, I don't know. So I saw it. I was there and I had access to that documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Bender. Mr. Scott, it seems to me that Mr. Bender is saying -- is talking about the records of the House of Representatives. I do not believe that they are what we are talking about. You are talking about the archive of the HZ HB, which is quite different, which would contain documents received by the political party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Judge Clark, that's absolutely correct. Although I must say I would be happy to receive information about any archive belonging to the HVO, the HDZ, Herceg-Bosna. I would be happy to hear any specific information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I think in fairness to the witness, because I'm being quite cross with him, we better be sure that he and the courts and you are talking about the same thing so first of all, can I continue before we do that, can the road where you say there was no name and no number, where was it close to? What was the nearest street that had a name? Which part of Mostar was it in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this, our premises, that is of the House of Representatives, were in the west side, on the west side, next to the Mostar hotel, and for a while, also in the -- on the premises of what was called the Hrvatski Dom, Herceg Stjepan Kosac, once again in the western part of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And when was the last time that you attended the House of Representatives on the west side next to the Mostar Hotel? Is that the ERO Hotel or the Mostar Hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. Hotel -- Mostar Hotel. I think Ero is a little bit further off and it's not there, so whilst the House of Representatives worked until the transfer of powers, I was physically there, and I had in my possession this documentation and had access to it. And I have already said that my secretary, or rather the secretary of the House of Representatives, discharged these duties and was responsible for the documents of the House of Representatives of the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The last time you were there, you say, was when power was handed over pursuant to the Dayton Accord. Where is the House of Representatives -- sorry, if that is so, do you know whether there was a hand-over of archives to the new governing body after the Dayton -- in accordance with the Dayton Accord?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not know, because our secretary was responsible for that. It was his job. So one should check with the secretary of the House of Representatives. He still discharges certain duties in the parliament of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. So I just do not know whether the documentation was handed over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bender. I really can't understand why you didn't give us all this information before. It doesn't seem to be classified information. Your witness now, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Clark.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, once again you've told us repeatedly that you are one of the senior officials among a small circling of the leadership. So I put these questions to you as someone who, based on that, I take it, would have -- might have information. Can you tell us, please, in light of what you've said about making request, can you tell us, please, why the HVO and the HDZ and those people that are still representing, as you call it, the Croats of Bosnia-Herzegovina, have not in fact produced documents at the request of the Prosecutor time after time after time since at least 1997?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, I don't know that the archives of the House of Representatives of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna has ever been asked for. If it had been asked I would have made sure that it was available both to the Prosecutor and to the Court, because it is public documentation. And as for the archive of -- archives of other institutions of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna and the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, you have to ask the leaders who held offices in the last mandate in the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna and it is very easy to find out who these people are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you have been one of the leaders. That's why I'm asking you. One of the general leaders. Perhaps not holding a particular office at a particular time, but you've told us repeatedly, you're one of the senior leaders of the Croats of Bosnia-Herzegovina -- excuse me, can I finish my question -- and that you just, until -- in the last days, literally days as we stand here now were being considered to be president of the HDZ BiH political party. It's on that basis that I put these questions to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, to a specific question the witness gave a specific answer. This is repetitive. I believe that the witness has provided a very specific answer to a very specific question. And the further insinuations refer to the year 2002. The witness has provided a very specific answer to a very specific question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, I guess the witness has answered your question. Probably he really doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I could ask one final question, Mr. President, and I will move on to the next topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll try to make it into one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, listen to my question please. To the extent you ever knowledge, can you please assist this Chamber with understanding why the officials of -- representing the Bosnian Croat part -- the Croatians of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that part of the federation, this jointly organised with the Muslims into the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, why the Croats from Bosnia-Herzegovina have not produced documents going back to 1997 and request -- in orders, binding orders from Judge McDonald, Judge Jorda and Judge May. Now, why haven't those orders ever been complied with?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But he has already answered that same question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that's the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Page 21, 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That's the specific question. Yes. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A very specific answer -- the archives of the House of Representatives that I'm responsible for, nobody has ever asked for. The archives of the government of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, you have to ask Mr. Jadranko Prlic and those who succeeded him, and as for the archives of the Croatian Defence Council, that so that is the military component, you ever to ask the Defence Ministry and the Chief of the Main Staff. I know that General Blaskic was there and who succeeded him, I don't know, but it's very easy to establish that. I don't want to do the guessing. So the responsible person who were there while the institutions were functioning, it is very easy to establish where the documents are, whether it has ever been asked for, why it has never been surrendered and if that is the case, these persons should be taken to task.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I said that would be my last question so I won't pursue it further. Mr. President, before I move on, this would be just an opportune moment. I said yesterday, in the course of the examination that I would provide the Chamber with the relevant portions of the 1991 census data, and those have been marked as Exhibits P109.1 and P109.2. And since they were first prepared and I'm sorry they are separate and will have to be reassembled, but they are the English translations of the columns of statistics so that the headings and categories -- can be read and understood by those not speaking Serbo-Croatian. They may come up in the further course the witness's testimony, but since they came up yesterday I told the Chamber I would provide this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before we move on to the questions relative to the statistics dating to 1992, I object because we do not have the integral statistical data. This is just an excerpt from a book or from a report. This is just one page. And this can be interpreted by an expert in demography. Lay persons cannot tell and understand anything from this one page. This is not an integral document. I believe that this book contains further explanations and instructions for lay people. Second point, Your Honours, the 1991, 1992 is marked by the largest migrations in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Without the help of experts, any examination regarding this document is a waste of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe that those documents are just for the reference purpose and if the Prosecution will tender these documents into evidence, I believe we have to see the original documents with the proper sources and the date. And it is not important issue at this stage. I thank you for your remarks, because if we admit those documents into evidence, when we are weighing these documents, we will take your views into full consideration. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, in connection with the formation of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, which you say you were one of the founders of, you attended a meeting in Grude on the 12th of November, 1991, correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hard to remember, but I assume I did. If you have a document, I would very much like to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this, and I will in a few moments but right now I'm just asking you some background questions. Is it correct, and I believe you said yesterday, that in your senior position, you participated in a number of meetings in connection with forming or establishing the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right. We had meetings, we had consultations, the leaders of the HDZ and a certain number of municipalities and we prepared the formation of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll ask the usher to please hand you what's been marked as IAC-2, and to save time, I'll also ask that -- these are not in the original bundle, but that Exhibits P101.1 -- I'll stop for the benefit of the Registrar, P101.1 which should be in the stack given to you today, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for bothering you again but I have to draw your attention to the fact that we have asked on a number of occasions that the documents -- if they are given in a binder like this, that we should be forewarned which documents would be used. I cannot carry tonnes of documents every day. I don't have a document IAC-2. I don't have it here and how am I supposed to follow? Why is it so difficult to forewarn us which documents are going to be used?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, I sympathise with you very much. Because we are in the same situation. We do not have those documents at our hands at first. I think as a principle, that we should be previously informed about the documents the Prosecution is going to use. Sometimes, during the cross-examinations, we could not prejudge what kind of document the party will use during their cross-examination. So there are some exceptions. Maybe Mr. Scott can give us a better explanation of that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, IAC-2 was in the bundle that was distributed yesterday. I think it's the last because they were put in numerical order and because there are some documents which have a different prefix such as the presidential transcripts being PT, and IAC, the international armed conflict documents also using the prefix IAC, they were put at the end. It's in the binder, Mr. President. Now that is not -- yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you. And you also furnished the documents P101.1 to the Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's what I'm just saying, Your Honour, yes, those two, 101.1 and 101.2 were not in the bundle yesterday they were only prepared over the evening and I've handed them out and provide them to the Registrar in coming into the courtroom today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, could I offer you a suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's time for a break. And I think you may direct the witness to get himself familiar with those documents, then when we come back, you can ask some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So we'll resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just a second, if I may. The Defence is of the position with regard to the practice that we have seen over the past several months in the courtroom, I would like to say that the Defence witnesses did not receive the same treatment as the witnesses for the Prosecution. This witness is here on -- of his own will to help the Court, and if he doesn't cope as well as he may, please do not treat him the way you do. There were witnesses who have refused, who said, "we don't want to answer your questions." They said that to both me and Mr. Seric and they were never warned as to what their duties are. This is what I wanted to say. As politely as I could. Because this is what has been known to happen in this courtroom. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I believe that this witness is an exceptional situation. Because the same question asked by you, yourself, by the Judges and by the Prosecution, for several times, but he did not answer that question. So we have to remind him of his obligation to answer questions and to remind him what was said in Rule 77. The witness has the obligation to answer questions. Earlier this warning was sent out as the last result. We'll try to persuade the witness to answer the question. If he doesn't know the answer, he will answer no. We will take it. There is no problem at all. I hope -- I hope when you are proofing your witness in the future, just remind the future witnesses about this point. Yes. Could we have the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may I add -- in this same courtroom, the same thing was said also to a number of witnesses for the Prosecution. Witnesses of the Prosecution were also told repeatedly that they had to answer questions. Whenever they seemed reluctant to cooperate properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, before the break, I asked three exhibits to be placed before you. My thanks to the usher. IAC-2, P101.1 and P101.2. And you were present at this meeting on the 12th of November, 1991, in Grude, weren't you, sir? And if it will assist you, you may wish to look at P101.1 and see if you can identify your name on the list of attendees. It may assist in the courtroom, Mr. Usher, if the English version could be put on the ELMO. It may just be easier than -- and for these purposes, Mr. Usher, could you please put the page of -- in the English version, it would be the third page, the third sheet of 101.1, if you could just put that on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, do you agree that in the list of names and of course I'll ask you to look at the Croatian language version, if you wish, but is that your name at item 17?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My name is here, and at first glance, this is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And looking at then the text of the document and for these purposes I'll look primarily to IAC-2, and looking at the last page of that document, either again, either the English version last page or the last page of the Croatian version, do you see that those -- that the meeting was chaired and these conclusions were signed by Mate Boban and Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do have this document, and as far as I can see, this document has not been signed either by Mr. Boban or by Mr. Kordic. At least the document that I have in front of me, and as far as I can remember, we always had a professional person taking minutes, so I suppose that my good friend, Jozo Maric, could not have been the person taking minutes. If you do have the document signed by Mr. Mate Boban and Mr. Kordic, we can discuss that document, and this, what I have in front of me is a paper that anybody could have written.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. I just do my job. This document was presented to various witnesses, to Bozo Raic and to Jozo Maric, and this paper as an integral part of this document, so this page was not there -- the page with the signatures, with the names of participants, but it doesn't say anywhere that this is an integral part of this document. This page was not presented before to any of the witnesses. The Defence claims that this page containing signatures is not the -- an integral part of this document. IAC-2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's hear what the witness is going to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me restate my question, sir. And you're absolutely correct. I should not have used the word signed. What I meant to indicate, this document -- this document indicates that in this meeting, it was chaired by Mr. Boban and Mr. Kordic and these conclusions were prepared over their typed names. I agree they don't bear, at least this document doesn't bear a hand signature but it's over the names of these two leaders of Croatians from Bosnia-Herzegovina, correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mate Boban and Mr. Dario Kordic were the leaders of the Croatian policy in Bosnia and Herzegovina. They are my good friends. However, Your Honours, in this document, which is not signed, I don't want to discuss this document, which is not signed, because anybody could have prepared this document. This is not an official document. This is IAC-2, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, did you attend this meeting, as reflected by the signature on P101.1 that I asked you about a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This paper that I have, under item 17, this is my signature at the first glance. However, this paper, this page, is not an integral part of this document that we are discussing, IAC-2. This is a separate page and this can be part of any other documentation or can be attached to any other documentation. Don't, please, attach this paper, this page, to what we are talking about, because I don't have the impression that this is its integral part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, this point has been pointed out by Defence counsel already. And the Prosecution just asked you a very simple question. Did you attend that meeting or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume. I can't remember that I was at the meeting on 12 November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I again apologise. I have to intervene. Can you please take the English version of IAC-2 and P101.2? And very -- it will be very easy for you to notice that the wording is identical, but in the document, item 1 does not show either Mr. Boban's name or Mr. Kordic's name. How is that possible? Absolutely identical text. So this is one and only document. Identical text, and it is identical in everything but in the person who took the minutes and Mr. Boban and Mr. Kordic, so an identical text --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: It's not an identical text, Mr. Krsnik. I looked at it particularly. It is different people writing different conclusions but dealing with the same subject. I looked at it very carefully over the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, incorrect. [Interpretation] In Croatian, Your Honour, no, I wouldn't rise to say no -- The Croatian text is absolutely the same, until the last comma. I don't -- my English is not as good but I believe that I'm right. Maybe we can consult with the interpreters to verify this. The Croatian -- the English text is completely identical. This is exactly my point. Your Honour, you don't seem -- you can't believe that I would say something that is not true?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, your view has been duly taken by this Trial Chamber. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have to say just before moving on on that, I don't understand the nature of Mr. Krsnik's objection. In the first paragraph of both 101.1 and IAC-2, unless we are looking at completely different documents, both Mr. Kordic and Mr. Boban are both named in the beginning paragraph of the document. But in any event ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that at this meeting, one of the -- would you consider this a historical meeting leading to the creation of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, an organisation which you've told us repeatedly now, since Tuesday, you were one of the founders of?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We held several meetings at which we discussed the organisation and preparations for the constitution of the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna. On the basis of the papers that I have before me, I do not wish to discuss papers which bear no signatures and which may not be official documents because casting a cursory look at the things that are here, there are a number of things that I disagree with.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, you can look at the documents or not. I'm going to ask you questions about the meeting. And perhaps even the series of meetings. If you don't want to talk about the specific documents, I'll ask you about meetings. Was it not the goal of the HDZ leaders and these Croatian members of Bosnia-Herzegovina, what they -- what you and others wanted to do was to achieve a lifelong and eternal dream, and that was a common Croatian state, Croatian state that extended and included the western part of Bosnia-Herzegovina? That was your objective, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not say so in our platforms and in our plans, and that is not my view. There were individuals in the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna, who held different views and had different suggestions. However, I shall repeat that no document, no decision, in its official part, in the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna and the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna, ever broached the subject in this manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, it was your objective and the outcome of this meeting, one of the conclusions reached in this meeting or, or these series of meetings, was that steps should be taken to proclaim a Croatian banovina in Bosnia-Herzegovina, correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct, and that is not true. Never, at the HDZ Bosnia-Herzegovina meetings or the meetings of the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna and the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna, was there ever a discussion were ever any decisions taken and place don't associate Croat Community Herceg-Bosna and Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna, with the Croatian banovina because these are two different ideas from two different periods of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, I put it to you, sir, and it's the Prosecution case that the Croatian Community Herceg-Bosna was indeed intended and steps were taken to implement that as to create the Croatian banovina and that's the Prosecution case, and I put that to you, sir. Was it not part of the goals of these series of meetings that the final solution would be gathering the Croatian people within the borders of a single, free Croatian state?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is what the Prosecutor alleges. I do not agree with that, because that was not in our objectives, our platforms, and we never discussed these matters in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, this meeting took place on the 12th of November, 1991, in Grude. Is it not true that six days later, on the 18th of November, 1991, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was proclaimed? The entity that you claim to be a founder of?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that on the 18th of November, 1991, in Grude, the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna was constituted and organised. You have documents, you have signatures. And what the documents say about the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna, these are our aspirations, these are our positions, rather than what somebody else says and what somebody else alleges. We -- I repeat, under full responsibility, under oath and before this Honourable Court, we saw and see Croat Community Herceg-Bosna and the Croat Republic Herceg-Bosna organised in a democratic way, as I have already said and let's not go back to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, when did you meet with anyone on behalf of Mr. Naletilic's defence in connection with coming here to testify?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regard to the testimony for the accused Naletilic, the Counsel called me and asked me if I would testify. There were some earlier calls and I stood by that. I said that I would testify in this case against Mr. Naletilic and Mr. Martinovic, and everybody else, because I consider myself responsible for the HDZ policies in Bosnia-Herzegovina, by that I mean the official policy of the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna and the Croatian Republic Herceg-Bosna, because I deem that there were no official omissions in our functioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecutor is asking you about the time. When did you meet with anyone on behalf of Mr. Naletilic's defence, if connection with meeting here to testify. It's just the time. Not the reason.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for that meeting, it was two or three months ago, I think, when the gentleman called me and we agreed that I would come to testify, and I repeat, I will testify in all the cases that deal with this, because I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How many times have you met with anyone on behalf of Mr. Naletilic in connection with coming to The Hague to testify?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe we met two or three times for a short time, and that we discussed and agreed on my testimony, and as for the policy and my position with -- in relation to this case that we are discussing now, I don't need Mr. Krsnik or anyone else, because I'm very familiar with all these matters, I'm an active actor, I'm an intellectual, I graduated in law and I feel responsible for the policy of the HDZ and the Croat Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Republic Herceg-Bosna. I mean the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That is, I do not need anybody's counsel, anybody's advice, anybody's help because I know all there is to know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you review this document before coming into the courtroom today, this IAC-2 or any other version of a record of the meeting in Grude on the 12th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The papers that I have been given, I do not remember having them, even though, perhaps, I do have some at home in my archive, but I certainly have a number of my papers, certain documentation dating back to that time. I do not recall seeing these papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Have you watched any of the proceedings in this case on television?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now and then, I watch television of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Now and then I watch the Croatian Television. Now and then I see some fragments from these cases. But specifically, I watched most because that is what was shown on television most, and that was the case against Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, for out of an abundance of caution, could we go to private session for a moment or two?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Bender, I recognise that 1991 is 11 years ago, and you say that you were at a number of meetings, you recognise that as being your signature but you don't necessarily recall that you were at this meeting in Grude. We'll move on from that. At meetings that you would attend on a regular basis, would it be common for somebody to be a minute-taker?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, minutes were kept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Would a minute-taker ever be asked to prepare a document where conclusions are arrived at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was natural to make an excerpt from the minutes and deliver it to people who were present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's not the question I asked you. I said would it be normal for the minute-taker who you recognised as a person of fairly low status, would it be normal in your circles for the minute-taker to draw conclusions and prepare a summary for distribution to people who were there? Or not there, as the case may be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said it. It was the routine and the duty to take -- to recapitulate the minutes, include the conclusions, and deliver it to people who had been present at the meeting, and then those people would discuss it at the next meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Bender, I think everyone here who attends meetings knows that frequently a summary of what happened is prepared and distributed. It is very unusual in my experience for the minute-taker to prepare the summary. Are you saying that where you operated, the minute-taker also prepared a summary? This person of lowly status?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You could see from the document, the minute-taker, in agreement with the President or chairman of the body, he prepares the conclusions he drafts the conclusions and delivers them to those present, to those present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Bender, I'm going to ask you the question in very simple terms again. Where you come from, does the lowly person, who is the minute-taker normally prepare a summary with conclusions of what happened at the meeting? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I repeat, in agreement with the president or chairman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The minutes are one document, and the conclusions are a second document. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Minutes is a book of lasting value, and it is kept in the archive, and an excerpt from the minutes, with the conclusions, is a separate document. That is how it was in our practice and that is how our practice still is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Do I understand you to say that you don't accept the conclusions that are contained in this document which purports, from the Prosecution point of view, to be a record of a meeting which took place in Grude in November, 1991? Is that what you're saying? That this is not a true document and that the contents are false?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document that I have and it is a document with these black numbers 00624 and 402 and 403, this is not the minutes, this is not a document from the meeting, this is not the document of this meeting. As far as I can know, somebody who read law, who was very active and who is now testifying here under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And are you saying that the contents are fabricated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot say whether that is the case or not. What I am saying is that it is not a true reflection, nor is it a summary of our discussions of our deliberations and conclusions at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Are the contents a misrepresentation, are false? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I disagree with the contents of the document. Therefore it was not adopted by our body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Bender, are you saying that the contents of those documents is a misrepresentation in material facts of what happened at that meeting? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this -- in these minutes, the facts are misrepresented. They are not represented correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what would happen normally when minutes of this meeting or any other meeting were kept and conclusions were arrived at? What would happen to those documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I repeat. Documents, minutes, were taken down in a notebook and they are kept, and must be kept, in the archive of the relevant body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So I take it that you, as a member of the Croatian community would, as a lawyer, have figured out that valid original documents are very important to assist this Tribunal in arriving at the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Original documents are of paramount importance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And you believe that these original documents exist somewhere, isn't that correct, from your previous testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe they do, because they simply must exist, but where they are, I'm not the leader of the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna, and therefore don't draw me into these details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Are you in a position in any way to assist the Defence and this Tribunal in seeing the minutes of these meetings? Because it's in the interests especially of Mr. Krsnik's clients and Mr. Seric's client that if documents which you accept as originals are available, that we should see them. Because what you're alleging, Mr. Bender, is that somebody is tampering with the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where the archive of the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna is, I have no personal knowledge of that, because I was not the front man, the leader of the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna and while the late Boban is not around any more, Mr. Dario Kordic, who was the vice-president, and Mr. Bozo Rajic should know where this archive is. I was specific, wasn't I? And I believe both these persons are available, because they are alive and we would also like to know the truth about this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: One last question, Mr. Bender. Is the archive not normally kept in a place which is safe for all citizens of a state rather than kept in the possession of a particular person who was in charge at the time? Are archives not objective and independent documents, which are kept safely for future generations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are right. The archive is kept in a manner prescribed, and I'm responsible for the archive of the House of Representatives, which is archived and which is kept in the manner prescribed. The official archive cannot be -- cannot be kept, cannot be in the hands of a private person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Why do you keep asking us to go to Mr. Kordic and to other people, like General Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I guess they know where the documentation is, of the bodies that they headed. Just as I have said that I knew where the archive of the House of Representatives was, and the secretary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, not Blaskic but the witness Bozo Rajic, the witness who testified here. You used the wrong last name. Mr. Bender said -- no, no, Bozo Rajic said, and you said General Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Earlier today he referred to General Blaskic, not in the last ten minutes, but earlier today this witness referred the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Earlier, yes, that's true, but now in answer to your question, he said Mr. Bodeso Rajic and Mr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me clarify it, Your Honour, I said and I will repeat, vice-president of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna were Mr. Dario Kordic and Mr. Bozo Rajic, because the president is not alive any longer, and I also mentioned Mr. Blaskic as the leader of the military components of the Croat Defence Council but that was earlier, not right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I deliberately referred to your earlier testimony? I said why do you keep referring us to people like Mr. Kordic and Mr. Blaskic when you know that they possible -- can't possibly be the archive keepers, that's the point I was making. I was referring to your earlier testimony. Thanks for answering my questions and I hope I don't have to put you on the spot again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, we will have to move on, of course, but before I do, let me ask you in terms of this, again the preparation of these documents, and the minute-taker or the recorder or what term you might wish to use. You are familiar with a man named Ignac Kostroman, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know him personally, Mr. Ignac Kostroman, I know personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: He was the general secretary of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna at the same time that Mr. Boban was president, Mr. Kordic was one of the two vice-presidents, correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that for a while, he was the general secretary or the secretary of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So, sir, if I simply can represent to you at the moment, if there are a substantial number of records of the Herceg-Bosna signed by Mr. Kostroman as the general secretary and keeper of the record of the meetings, you would say, I guess, is it correct, that would be beneath Mr. Kostroman?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kostroman is alive. You can go to him and ask him, and as for -- as far as documents are concerned, I can discuss documents that I have an opportunity to see and study.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm asking the question to you, sir. Mr. Kostroman signing or preparing minutes and records of meetings, according to you, would be beneath somebody such as Mr. Kostroman; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kostroman is the secretary, so he is responsible for all the matters that are under his -- the scope of his duties. And that includes the minutes, filing of various documents, together with the leading people of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to put it to you one last time and then I will certainly tell the Chamber that I'm going to move on. We put it to you, sir, I know you don't agree, but we put it to you, for instance that Mr. Jozo Maric was involved in this historic meeting and that it would have been in fact a point of honour by someone such as yourself or Mr. Maric or Mr. Kostroman to put their name on such a historic document as this. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't say that. I said that the minute-taker was not a -- at the time, it was not the practice at the time that a minute-taker would be a mayor of any municipality. Mr. Jozo Maric in this particular case was the mayor of Grude and it doesn't make sense that he would be the one to take the minutes, and I can't see his signature here, and Mr. Jozo Maric is alive, and I sincerely hope that it is not too difficult to go to him and ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I could ask the usher to please hand you Exhibit P114? Which is in the bundle, Mr. President. And was previously admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, sir, who Ivan Markesic was?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivan Markesic -- Ivan Markesic was the general secretary of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina. He is alive. You can get to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, my questions are to you and it will not assist us, I submit to you respectfully, to tell us who else might be available. You're in the courtroom and I'm directing my questions to you, sir. What was the role and responsibilities of Mr. Markesic as the general secretary of the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: During his mandate, while he was the general secretary of HDZ BH, he was in charge of administrative and other affairs in the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina, so he had all the secretarial duties which are described in our statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, would it be part of his duties that this topic take we have been on now for sometime to keep the records and the official documents of the HDZ BiH?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He could do that, but I assume that -- that the records were taken by somebody else and then he was the one who assisted with compiling the conclusions and preparing the summary of a particular meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, please, who is Andjelko Stojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Andjelka Stojic and not Andjelko Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apologies, who is Andjelka Stojic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Mrs. Stojic, who at that time was not married. She was an employee of the secretariat of the HDZ, BH. She returned -- she had returned from Australia. Highly educated person, speaks foreign languages, and she lives in Stolac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: She lived in Stolac. She lives there again? You're speaking in the present tense, she lives in Stolac today or she lived in Stolac at the time or both?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: She still lives in Stolac, because she is married there and her name now is Andjelka Raguz and at this particular time she lived in Sarajevo. I don't know where she was during the war. I can't follow everybody's tracks but currently she resides in Stolac, she is married and she I think has three or four children.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, sir, if I can direct your attention to -- forgive me -- sorry -- page 3? I'm trying to assist you, sir, in making sure, looking at the Croatian version as well. There is a group, there is a list of names that talk about the persons who were involved in the discussion, and in the Croatian version, I believe it's also on the third page, so if you could look at that, please?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the list, and I can also see my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And will you agree with me, sir, that you were at this meeting and that you indeed participated in these discussions?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot claim that I was or that I wasn't, but I assume that I was at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, why do you assume that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it is just a matter of the time that has lapsed and I can't remember all the meetings and all the dates where I was during 1992, and that is exactly the same, that is exactly true of any other person.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And sir, that would be true, would it not, then, of all your testimony in direct examination as well? You just don't remember any details of any of these things, do you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember some things and I don't remember some others. And that is why the Honourable Court is here to discuss things and to arrive at an agreement and I'm under oath, and I just tell you the things that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, at this meeting, and the purpose of this meeting, is it not true, was because the HDZ wanted a different form of the referendum question, correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said when I was asked by Defence Counsel Krsnik that we did determine at our meeting in Livno the proposal of our question for the referendum and that we submitted to the Republican Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir, on page 2, at the bottom part of the half of the page, you will find, I believe, the referendum question as prepared by the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which states, "Are you in favour --" and the letter or the word "of" appears to be missing I'll just read it literally as it states, "Are you in favour a sovereign and independence Bosnia and Herzegovina, a state of equal citizens and peoples, Croats, Muslims, Serbs, and other peoples who live in it?" That was the question as formulated by the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina, correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I was at this assembly session and more or less this is what was established at the republican assembly session which was held on 24, 25 and 26 January, of 1992, in Sarajevo. And the minutes can be obtained if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the proposition that the HDZ people as gathered in this meeting which this record tells us there were 147 people in attendance and that 140 of the 147 approved this alternative formulation which says, "Are you in favour of a sovereign and independent Bosnia and Herzegovina, a joint state of the constitutive and sovereign Croatian, Muslim and Serbian peoples, in their ethnic areas or in cantons?" That was the form of the proposition or referendum approved -- referendum approved at this gathering, correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this particular meeting in Livno we adopted the proposal of the referendum question and as far as I can remember, this is more or less identical to what it says here, but let us look at these two questions. They differ in as much as in the proposal that the HDZ established also refers to the future organisation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and I don't see anything disputable here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, when you added the phrase "after a joint state of the constitutive and sovereign Croatian Muslim and Serbian peoples," in that sentence or that parts of the phrase that says "sovereign" why did this group of people insert the word "sovereign" at that point?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe there is nothing disputable here in terms of the word "constitutive and sovereign peoples" because this is what we have been talking about all the time. This is what we are discussing here, and these words are absolutely acceptable, because our proposal of the question for the referendum, we submitted to the assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina. If you are interested in this, we will go back to that. We will -- I can tell you what -- how we behaved at the referendum and what we did. This was submitted to the assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina and we have never received an answer to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... listen to Judge Clark's questions, please listen to my question.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What did you mean by adding and for what purpose was the phrase "their ethnic areas" why was that added?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This -- this was the wording of our question because we were talking about the future organisation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How would these peoples, these three peoples listed here, how was it they would be organised in their ethnic areas?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, Your Honours, we still have our counties or cantons, which are organised on the principle of a majority Croat, Muslim or Bosniak population, in the interior of -- in the area of the federation, unfortunately we haven't done that in Republika Srpska. Q.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'd like the usher's assistance please to put before the witness at one time to save time, Exhibit P271 which was a previously admitted exhibit, P-- that's P271, and in the new bundle of documents you should find P239.2, P348, P349. I would also ask to you please put before the witness, I'm sorry, P39.1. There are five. I believe that's a total of five exhibits, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you first, please, to direct your attention to P271. Sir, you've told this Chamber in your testimony that you believe or you know, you have some basis for your testimony, for asserting that President Izetbegovic signed this document even though his signature is not reflected here. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember my testimony. I confirm this, because the late Mate Boban told me, but not only to me, but he said that at a meeting, that both Mr. Izetbegovic and himself adopted -- had adopted and signed this statement. And I hope that there is a document to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, that was my question to you, sir. As part of these documents, as part of the HDZ archive, have you ever seen a document that has Mr. Izetbegovic's signature on it? That you can assist us with?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, I have not seen it, but I believe -- I believe that the late president Mr. Mate Boban, when he said that this had been signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
