utterances.text: So just before we move forward, sir, the entire basis for your assertion under oath that Mr. Izetbegovic signed this joint statement, alleged joint statement, is what Mate Boban told you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe Mr. Boban because he is a man of honour, whose word is his bond, and we were good friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you'll direct your attention -- I'm only focusing you this so I can put some additional questions to you but paragraph 3 of Exhibit 271, the latter part of that section or paragraph 3 says, "And in the provinces 3, 8 and 10, under the command of the general staff of the HVO" and I'm sorry I should have backed up to say, "The armed forces of the HVO and the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina," then skipping back to what I just referred you to, "In the provinces 3, 8 and 10 would be placed under the command or were to be placed under the command of the general staff of the HVO."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I waited for us to move on. Is it not the time to ask the Prosecutor how did this document -- how come that this document, with something added on top of the document, "Boban's proposal," it is? And the previous document that I had been given, lacks that addition by hand? I waited until the end of the question. I didn't want to interrupt. This is the same document. One of them has an addition by hand. That's what you have in your binder. A previously, we had received the same document without the words added by hand. Who was it who added these words by hand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott, could you give us an explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, Exhibit P271, that we have in our binder, and I will ask the usher's assistance, the Registrar's assistance, Exhibit P271 has that on the top of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand this document has already been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In your case-in-chief. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And when we adopted -- admitted that document, you mean that those words were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, subject to verification by the Registrar, Your Honour, that's my understanding. Yes, I can see it from here. It's on the document. The words -- the items that Mr. Krsnik say were not on the document are on the document as tendered and as previously admitted by this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, there should be no problem on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really -- it's beyond me. This is what I received from the Prosecutor, and it does not contain the words "Boban's proposal." So this is really beyond me. I don't understand what the matter may be here because this is the document that I prepared, and that I took from the binder that I had received. And last night, when I was checking my documents, I actually used this document in my direct examination, and I immediately I noticed the difference because this is the document, the one that I have, that I used in my examination of Mr. Bender.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we should be governed by the official records of the Court kept by the Registrar. I think that resolves the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, we have noticed that point that you made on this very issue. And we -- when we are evaluating those documents, we will take it into consideration. Yes, Mr. Scott, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I simply want to explain to you and to the Chamber now in directing your attention to 2.39.2 -- sorry, excuse me, Your Honour. Mr. President, what I'd like to do and I do this so everyone in the courtroom will know what I'm referring to. In 239.1, which is also previously admitted in evidence, on page -- using the original page numbers that were at one point put on the UN document, if the Chamber could find page 2 and the others could find page 280, toward the very back, almost at the back of the document, page 280?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Scott, do you mean P239.2?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: At the moment, I mean 239.1, the original document which was in the binders and which was admitted -- perhaps for ease of reference for the courtroom, Mr. Usher, if you could put page 280 on the ELMO? And I'm particularly interested in the technical booth assisting us by focusing on item E, "Withdrawal of forces." Please zoom in on that as much as you can. Now, Mr. President, you will see that what we have done in 239.2 is simply take that part, subsection, and to assist and to comply with the Chamber's practice and to assist the witness I've had several of these particular provisions translated and which are attached.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I hope in the future, you could make some notes before this document, that is 239.2, so that we could easily found out those excerpts, those parts of that document you produced to facilitate the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, on our list you'll note P239.2, excerpt of P239.1. So we have attempted to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd like you -- and you can look at the Serbo-Croatian version that's attached, I'm looking at subsection called E, "Withdrawal of forces." You can look at that. I will refer to the English version. Sir, does it not say, "Sarajevo province shall be immediately demilitarised, all Serb forces shall withdraw in provinces 2, 4 and 6; HVO forces into province 3; Bosnian army forces into province 1. Both Bosnian army and HVO forces shall be deployed in provinces 5, 8, 9 and 10, under arrangements agreed between them." Now, I want to you look at that, sir, and since you say that you're knowledgeable of these things and that you say that you know that Mr. Izetbegovic supposedly signed this document, can you tell me, sir, where in section E, which was signed -- which indeed was signed by Mr. Izetbegovic and Mr. Boban on the 25th of March, 1993, as reflected in the UN Security Council documents, where in that provision does it say that the provinces -- that the forces of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina will be placed under HVO command in provinces 3, 8 and 10?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact is that these two documents are not identical, that the wording is different, but please don't involve me in any military contexts or structures, I'm not a military expert. I only said that I remember, this is exactly what I said to counsel Krsnik, that I do remember this joint statement and I'm just conveying the words of Mr. Boban. Personally I don't know what the matter was. But I'm just conveying what was said to me, that Mr. Mate Boban and Mr. Izetbegovic signed this joint statement that we are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm putting to you, sir, that [Microphone not activated] Translation continues] ... did not sign it, but supporting a proposition, putting the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina under the command of the HVO, when that was exactly contrary or not supported at all in the document that he had indeed did sign on the 28th of March? And my question is, you've told us you're a trained man, you're an intellectual, you're a lawyer, so please look at the language of E, "Withdrawal of forces," and tell me what support you find in that provision for Mate Boban's statement in paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said that these two texts are not identical, that they are very different, but I stand by my statement that was told me by Mr. Boban, and as for the withdrawal of forces in item E, I repeat I'm not a military expert, I'm not a military man, so don't put me into the army. I'm a politician, a lawyer, and ask me about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see the time and it's probably the break time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I once again waited for the end of the question, but again, there was a misrepresentation, because it says clearly that in provinces 5, 8 and 9 and 10, under arrangements agreed between them, that is the HVO and the BH Army. It says agreed between them. So it was left to them to reach an agreement about it. And this was done on the 2nd of April. I merely waited for the Prosecutor to finish because I didn't want to be cautioned once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your explanation on those documents. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I won't follow up now. The Chamber wants to take a break. I'll come back to it after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could I know how long are you going to take for your cross-examination? Are we going to finish the testimony of this witness today?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, we will finish the cross -- yes, Your Honour, I believe so. I can finish the cross examination, I think, before 7.00, but how long the other questions may be of course I can't predict. I will finish my cross-examination today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, and leave us sometime to ask questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour. I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll resume at quarter to 6.00

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I apologise but I wish to indicate some other problems that have to do with the translation or interpretation? I did not pay attention that the transcript said that Mr. Bender was a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But he is not a lawyer. I asked my colleagues who live in the United States and speak Croatian what do you call a man who graduates from law? What kind of a title does he have in and he told me that the closest would be to the European spirit of language is JD, jurisprudence doctor, but that in the States, they can also call them lawyers, but they are not barristers. When we say a graduated lawyer in Croatia we mean a man who read and graduated from law. And that is what Mr. Bender said. He did not say that he was a barrister. He is not an advocate. He is a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, the points here is not whether the witness is a lawyer or not. The problem is that we were told that during the break, the witness talked to your client. I believe it is your obligation to inform your witness beforehand, "Don't talk to anybody." Including your client, when he was still under the oath. This is for the future witnesses. Yes. Could we have the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Just on a point of information, Mr. Krsnik, our country is also part of Europe and we would make a distinction between a lawyer who would either be a solicitor or a barrister and a law graduate and when you say somebody is a law graduate, you mean he's using his law degree to assist him in business or whatever, but that he's not a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is not here. I thought that you were part of the legal system of -- Anglo-Saxon law, in which you are barristers and solicitors and I thought that you had three degrees, law graduate, solicitor, barrister. I know that it is accessible to you but I was just told that he is not an advocate. He is not a solicitor or barrister and then I asked how it was in America and I found out how they do these things. But thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I think in America they are usually called corporate lawyers. In other words they never set foot in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We don't consider them real lawyers, Judge Clark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, before moving off this topic, I would like you to look at Exhibit -- and really you can look at either one that suits you -- 349 -- actually I take that back, I think for your purposes, sir, you would look at P348, the back of which you will find a Croatian version. I would suggest to the Chamber that just because the legibility of the two documents, the English version, P349, the last page of that exhibit is I think more legible. I represent to the Chamber that the text is identical and I'm sure I'll be corrected if I'm wrong. At the back of page -- Exhibit P348 there is a Serbo-Croatian version of the document. Now, sir, I just want to ask you, would you look at that last page, it is an attachment to this joint statement, indeed again this one bearing the signature of Mr. Izetbegovic and Mr. Boban and others, on the 25th of April, two weeks later, and I'll just ask you to scan your eyes please down paragraphs 1 through 5, and I ask you again, is there anything in that statement which supports Mr. Boban's -- we put it to you, "ultimatum" that the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina subordinate itself to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Prosecutor, I do not see here -- I'm not a military expert, I do not know what Mr. Boban's "ultimatum" you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, doesn't -- I'll move on very quickly but in the document I just showed you and directed your attention to paragraph number 1. I'm not going to take the time to read the whole thing but doesn't that make it very clear that the BiH Army, and I'm is simply using the terms in the document, that the BiH Army and the HVO will retain their separate identities and command structures?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You read it correctly, but once again, army, that is not my field. I am not a military expert. Mr. Milivoj Petkovic is alive. Mr. Sefer Halilovic is alive, so call them and clear the matter up with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm only asking because you've testified under oath that you believe and have asserted as a fact to this Chamber that Mr. Izetbegovic signed the document dated 2nd April, 1993, marked as P271, and I put it to you, sir, that the documents that indeed he did sign, which I've shown to you this afternoon, provide no support for the ultimatum issued by Mr. Boban. Now, that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I did not mention any ultimatum, the joint statement that we talked about of the 2nd of April, I said that not only I, but a number of us were informed, that Mr. Izetbegovic and Mr. Mate Boban had signed that joint statement. I do not wish to change it because there, is nothing to change. And as for this, I do not really know what Mr. Petkovic and Mr. Halilovic signed. They are here. Call them and clear it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm sorry, I was also waiting for the end. There is a document, it's once again misrepresented and I believe we have agreed that this may not be done in cross-examination. Because this joint statement that is before us and that you have states clearly, in which provinces will the forces be subordinated to the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and which to the HVO. And they also undertake to form the joint command by the 15th of April and all that pursuant to Vance-Owen Plan and it all says nicely here. Then why is a document misinterpreted and why is Mr. Boban's "ultimatum"? No Boban's "ultimatum" is mentioned but it says after the conclusion of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, Alija Izetbegovic and Mate Boban, I agree, pending full demilitarisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina as envisioned by the peace plan and with a view to more efficient defence against the aggression -- I'm sorry. The armed forces of the HVO in provinces 1, 5 and 9 are being placed under the command of the general staff of the army of BH. And in the provinces 3, 8 and 10 under the command of the general staff of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, whatever is said in this document, we can read by ourselves. And I think your witness has answered the question put by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, but please instruct me, one may not misinterpret and thus mislead the witness. There is no trace of Boban's "ultimatum" and therefore a document is misrepresented to him and he's asked to answer. Then it would be fair to let him read it through, all the items, and then for the Prosecutor to ask him a question rather than misleading completely and putting to him things that these documents don't say. It's not fair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, in this case, I don't think it's misleading. Your witness could answer that question according to his own knowledge. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, just to be clear I put all those documents in front of the witness, gave him time, asked him to look at them, and I put the Prosecution's case to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with an organisation called the association of volunteers and veterans of the homeland war?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that institution in our territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you remember attending the first regular session of that association?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember whether I attended meetings of this association, because we had quite a number of such associations. So I cannot really confirm that I was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, do you remember attending the first regular session of this association along with the following persons, Mr. Miro Grabovac, Dario Kordic, Tihomir Blaskic, Jadranko Prlic, Vladimir Suljic and Tomislav Mercep?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard of those people but I do not remember that I attended a joint meeting with them, so that I cannot confirm that I was at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, that a man named Ivan Andabak is the president of that -- something part of that organisation called the "court of honour"?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, could I have the transcript back on the screen? I don't have the text on the screen. Please. Could the Prosecutor repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course. Are you familiar, sir, or are you aware of the fact that a man named Ivan Andabak is indicated as the president of the "court of honour" of that organisation, whatever that might be?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know how this organisation -- how this association is organised. I've heard about Mr. Andabak. However, what office, what duties he discharges in that association, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll ask to you look at Exhibit P927 -- it should be in the bundle of documents, it's either -- it may have been distributed, Madam Registrar, I'm not sure if it was today or yesterday, I may have given it to the usher. If it wasn't yesterday, then it may have been -- thank you very much. P927. Sir, I represent to you and for the record that what I put to you comes from a publication called Obrana [phoen] Herceg-Bosna written by Karlo Ratim [phoen], in Siroki Brijeg, published in 1997. You can look at the Croatian version if it will assist you. If I can direct you to look at the paragraph on page -- of the Croatian version, 609, and the paragraph of text immediately above the table 6.2.1? If you look at that for a moment, sir, does that assist your memory at all in attending that first regular session of that organisation?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that the paper said so, that Ivan Bender was present, yes, it does say so, but I cannot confirm it. Because this is a book, I'm aware of its existence, I'm aware that it was published but it need not be reliable. I cannot remember that I was present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, and can you assist the Chamber in confirming, that one of the accused in this case, Mladen Naletilic, also known as Tuta, is the lifelong honorary head or chairman of that organisation?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard that the members of the association elected Mr. Mladen Naletilic to that office. If they did that in a democratic way, then I have no problem with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with the situation where much of the international community considers the association of volunteers and veterans of the homeland war to be one of the most anti-Dayton organisations in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What the international community thinks or representatives of international community think in relation to this association is not something that I am aware of, but this association exists in the lands of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is Bosnia and Herzegovina. It has its leadership and if my memory serves me well, the organisation is headed by Mr. Miro Grabovac, so you can communicate with him and talk with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, whether, since Mr. Naletilic has been in detention in The Hague, does he continue to be the lifelong honorary chairman of this organisation?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, don't ask me that. Ask members of the association. And ask its president, Mr. Miro Grabovac. I do not know that. That is not within my jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Bender, you were asked did you know, and you can say, "No, I don't know" or "yes, I do know." Don't ask the Prosecution to ask someone else. You can answer whether you know or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said it clearly, I do not know, and I also said where that information could be obtained. I am not aware of that fact, that is that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware of the fact that in about early April, 2001, the international community, through both the Office of the High Representative and through the stabilization forces of the United Nations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, so far, I never objected to any Prosecutor's question when he tried to challenge the credibility. But does this Honourable Court and the Defence really believe that the implementation of the Dayton Peace Accords is a -- within the terms of reference of this Tribunal? Is it the responsibility of this Tribunal? What kind of a question is it? We have the indictment. I never raised that matter before. We are speaking -- spending 80 per cent of the time talking about post-Dayton Bosnia, who is pro, who is anti-Dayton and so on and so forth. And what do they said to prove this? Bosnia was definitively divided in Dayton and it's going through its post-Dayton period of time and crisis and experience in this way are another. And what does this have to do with this Chamber or this Tribunal and what is the relevance of all these things? Why do we have to listen to that hour after hour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, the Prosecution has not finished his question. Let him finish that question. And your remarks have been noted by us. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware that in early April, 2001, representatives of the office of the high representative and of SFOR conducted an investigation of a bank in Bosnia-Herzegovina called the Hercegovacka Bank [phoen], with its main office in Mostar, but also offices in Grude in which there was violent resistance to this investigation, and in fact a number of people, representatives of the international community, were injured?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to this, for the record. Your Honours, it is an incident unheard of in the civilisation, in the modern history of the world, of the whole globe, I do not know who did the Prosecutor learn about it, where did he get the information and positions that he's voicing here, that he's referring to, when a private institution was robbed and to this day, the proceedings have not been completed, because of this act which was committed, and what does that have to do with this case, and this witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that's exactly the question we want to know. Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I asked the Chamber to take notice of the word that Mr. Krsnik just used, when the bank was robbed. It was an action, an operation carried out by the office of the high representative and SFOR, under the authority of the Dayton peace accords.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you were familiar with that fact and in fact, didn't you appear when some of these events were happening in Grude at the branch of the bank in Grude, after the events were over, you said "the international community has been defeated"?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is regrettable that the Prosecutor is not telling the truth. What the Prosecutor said is not true. The press, and some representatives, did say that, but it was denied. And I claim under full responsibility that on that day, the 6th of April, 1991, I was not in Grude for the whole 24 hours. I was in my office in Mostar, in the administration for pensions and pension insurance and social welfare. I am surprised that the Prosecutor resorts to such insinuations and attributes them to me. And as for the breaking of the SFOR forces in their tanks into a bank, I claim under full responsibility that it was not done in a regular manner, and to avoid any misunderstanding, on the 6th of April, at this time, at that time, throughout, I was in Mostar all day long. I never -- I never set my foot in Grude. The Prosecutor is not telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, the question asked by the Prosecutor is after the events were over, you said that "the international community has been defeated." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is not true. I was not in Grude. I did not say that. These are not my words.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have to finish and I'll go on. I put the question to the witness and I'll just go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I ask the witness please be provided -- and these are my last set of questions, exhibits -- in the interests of time, both PT 33, presidential transcript number 33 and presidential transcript number 35, which I'll only touch on briefly. I suggest that the easiest way of dealing with this material in the English material, Mr. President, is just to put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'd first like to address your attention as we are assembling this material -- I'm sorry, I'm sorry, you don't have it. If I can first ask you to look at Exhibit PT35? Which I will state, is a record of a meeting at the offices of the President Franjo Tudjman of Croatia on the 24th of November, 1995, I only have one question about this document -- well, two. Now, sir, you can scan your eyes down through the document if you wish but I will represent to you, sir, can you confirm that you were in attendance at this meeting in the offices of the president on the 24th of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is 24 November, 1995, I could not have attended that meeting. I already said that, because on that day, I was visiting a good friend of mine in Dubrovnik. I remember the date very well. It was on the 24th November, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask if we could have the Croatian original on the ELMO so that we can establish the date, because this -- you can't see on the transcript, it could be 1995 or 1996, because somebody subsequently corrected the figure. If you don't have the Croatian original, can we put it on the ELMO so you can actually see it for yourself because you can't actually tell the year when the meeting was held. If the Prosecutor alleges the meeting was held in 1995, okay, I will agree to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is the form -- I can only represent this is the form in which the document was received, through the channels that you're familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you've said yesterday that, I believe I'm almost reminded from the context of the events of the discussion, we would submit, Your Honours, would indicate, 1995. Sir, yesterday, one of the things you told Mr. Krsnik was that these transcripts could not possibly -- could not be accurate because they did not reflect your style and manner of speaking and one of the things you objected to was that the length of the statements or passages attributed to you. Do you remember that? Do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We discussed all of these transcripts, and I made a note for my own information, that there were five of them, and in agreement with Honourable Court, I had the opportunity to look at them in my hotel room, and I confirm that what I said was correct, and as far as this transcript goes, I don't know whether this was the year 1995 or 1996. If it was 1995, I said, and I repeat, I will stick to my statement, that as far as I can remember, the meetings with President Tudjman, they were always very short and clear, because there was not a very much on the agenda, not very much to discuss. It was just to receive information and go back to the HZ HB or HR HB and deal with the issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you told us yesterday that one of the reasons that you asserted that this could not be authentic is the length of the comments attributed to you. In fact, sir, isn't it true you had quite the reputation for making quite long remarks, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what you say. I haven't heard that, as a person with a degree in law, there is no need for me to go at length. Mathematics is also one of my professions, so if we sort of join together mathematics and law this is what we receive and this is, I believe that I behave in this manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bender, of course the Chamber will be able to make its own assessment of the length of your answers and responses as well, but let me direct your attention, please, to, in your version, page -- and I'm going to refer to page, sir, that are in the upper right corner in the Croatian version, if you could please find page R0159369? And for the English readers, in Exhibit P35, if I can direct you please to the same page reference to R010416? If the English version could be put on the ELMO, Mr. Usher, the last four digits being 0416.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, is it not correct that at that -- during that meeting and you're indicated as the next speaker after this passage, in fact, that Gojko Susak, the minister said, "Mr. President today I drew the conclusion since there was a meeting with you in a very serious tone when we went to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. lunch I said to everyone present that they have to learn from Bender what it means to be a politician to speak for half an hour and not say anything. And they all had a good laugh, you know, and then, after lunch we came back and he asked for the floor. And said the same thing in a different way and confirmed that he's the greatest politician among them. He's asking for the floor." Next entry, Ivan Bender, "Mr. President I'd like to try to refute what our minister said." Now, sir, you had quite the reputation for making long remarks, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what you claim. I can't confirm that. This is indeed what it says here, but what is under the name Ivan Bender, does not correspond to my way of work, primarily, as a person with all the personal traits that I have, I cannot refer to the late minister Susak as "our minister." Our defence minister at the time was Vladimir Soljic, and I know Vladimir very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you, you used the term "our minister" quite deliberately and that in fact shows exactly what your state of mind was in November, 1995.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can claim that but I cannot accept that, and I deny that energetically and I stick to my claim. At that time our defence minister was Vladimir Suljic and the late minister Gojko Susak was the minister in the government of the Republic of Croatia. So these are two different posts and two different persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask to you look at Exhibit PT33, please, the next transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am making an effort and this is my last series of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall being at a meeting in the offices of Franjo Tudjman on the 27th of March, 1995? Along with a delegation from Herceg-Bosna, Dario Kordic, Jadranko Prlic, Pero Markovic, Bozo Raic, Jozo Maric? Do you remember being in a meeting with all those people, with President Tudjman?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a number of meetings, I've already said that, and if my memory serves me well, it is to be assumed that I was in this meeting on the 27th March, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that you and the attendees at this meeting, including Franjo Tudjman, knew that the establishment of cantons under the Washington Agreement presented problems for the HDZ cause because they would be based on parity and not on HVO control?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The establishment of counties, i.e. cantons in our area in the area of the federation, had and still presented -- and still presents a lot of problems. But we have been dealing with these problems and these are for a while now have been functioning as they should.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you knew, and it was discussed in this meeting that the cantons were a problem and in fact they were directly contrary to the whole concept and purpose of the Croatian community and later the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what you claim. I cannot confirm your claim, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... attention please to page 8572 in your Croatian version, please look at the last four digits, the number that's in the upper right corner of the pages, sir, 8572.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And Mr. Usher, if you could please put on the ELMO in the English version the last four digits would be 0327. The English version, please, Mr. Usher, 0327. If I could have the technical booth with the paragraph with the words starting, "We have reached a critical," if you can zoom in on the upper right corner of the document now? That's fine. But if the technical booth can close in on that a bit? All right. That's fine. Well, I'd like everyone to be able to read it as much as possible of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, did President Tudjman not say, sir, "We have reached a critical point" -- my apology, I believe this is Dario Kordic speaking, "We have reached a critical point when even this leadership, that has come, finds it difficult to make the right moves certainly not without your help and the support of the Croatian people. So we think that the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna should be a guarantee of the survival of the Croatian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina but there are some contradictions and defeatism is spreading amongst the people." Because of time, sir, I'm going to skip down a few lines. When Mr. Kordic goes on to talk about the problems presented, in the next paragraph, "It is important that we do our part and in so doing show the international community what we have done, above all in the cantons with parity, based on the 1990 electoral results. We clearly have some problems here because the parity-based contents -- cantons," my apology, "... the parity based cantons bring the very position of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna into question." Do you remember discussing that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have read something, but I don't have that, this text. Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we don't have it either. I don't want to intervene but on the page the Prosecutor has mentioned and page 572, I don't see that there is no this text. I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Usher, please make sure that the witness has that document. How about the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Are you saying you don't have it in Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Because it's here in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: It's in English but in B/C/S it doesn't have what the Prosecutor is reading.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I have in Croatian is not what the Prosecutor has just read.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, give me a moment, I'll see if I can sort it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you'll look at page, if you'll find, please, page, the last four digits, 8572, and in the upper left corner of the Croatian version, there is the other, additional markings, a 2/1, and then the initials LJ. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have this page. It's in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, at the top of that page, sir, do you not see, and it may be that it starts on the previous page, but do you not see the part of the passage that I just read to you? Look at page, I'm sorry, I'm trying to move quickly. Would you look at the previous page then 8571, sir? And I suggest to you you'll find the words there.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat one passage so that I can see where I am on this page?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The part that I direct your attention to started with this, attributed to Mr. Kordic, if you want to look you can even look back a page earlier to 8570 and you will see where Mr. Kordic begins speaking and continuing over in the Croatian version, to page --

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have that text.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. Wasn't it discussed, sir, at this meeting that you and Dario Kordic and Jozo Maric and Bozo Raic and Franjo Tudjman were at, wasn't it discussed that this was a problem because the parity-based -- I'm quoting now that because the parity based cantons bring the very position of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna into question?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, you mentioned a name, Bozo Maric. I don't recall that person, such a person was never among us, and as far as Mr. Dario Kordic's words, I can't remember what he was talking about. The man is alive. Ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, we've done this all afternoon, sir. I'm asking you. Isn't it true that you're at this meeting, which must have some moment for you, you're meeting with the president, sitting president, of the Republic of Croatia, and you do not remember talking about this and that this present and serious problem for you, for the very project, the very project we put to you, that you'd been so closely involved in since 1991? And it was at risk because the cantons under Dayton or under Washington excuse me, would be based on parity?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the things that I don't want to repeat. We attended several meetings in the offices of the President of Croatia, Dr. Tudjman, who informed us and, so to say, gave us his opinion about the overall situation. There were problems with the organisation of counties but we solved them and it functioned. So that we, the Croats, and Bosniaks in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina have agreed on the -- on these things, and we enforce the Dayton Accords. We constituted the counties --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I have to finish. Sir, isn't it true that Franjo Tudjman expressed in this meeting that he would have preferred three -- a union of three republics, being a Croat Republic, a Serb Republic and a Muslim republic, and in fact that's the position that you would have preferred, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What the President Tudjman said I can't remember. And what I would prefer or what somebody else would prefer, we can discuss that but the fact is what we did officially and what we adopted officially, the Dayton Accord and its implementation is something that both the Croatian community and the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna and federation did together and implemented together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to look in your Croatian version at page 8628 using the numbers that we have been using.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just briefly I would still like to find out, to see where the Prosecutor found the previous text that he read in English. I'm still trying to find it in Croatian and I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I took the witness right to it and no, I don't speak, regrettably, Serbo-Croatian, I think I can say with confidence I took the witness right to it and the witness found it. The witness found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, could we solve this issue after the Court? Because we have passed this period.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I want you to look now, please, at 8628.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And Mr. Usher, if you could put on the ELMO, in the English version, 0378? The bottom of that page, please, 0378.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, toward the bottom, in that section attributed to President Franjo Tudjman and in the English, I can only say in the English version toward the bottom of page 378, did not Mr. Tudjman say -- President Tudjman say, "And I said that if it had been possible to implement that agreement on the union of three republics, that would have been the best for the Croatian state in the present historical circumstances but the western world did not accept that." Now, do you remember that statement?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember these words, and this statement, because it was a long time ago. We had a number of meetings. My memory and, so to say, my modest brain cannot recall all these things. So I cannot confirm these words that the Prosecutor has just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it correct that President Tudjman and the others, in fact, in terms of any settlement, you didn't want parts of Bosnia that would have more Muslims and more Serbs, correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct. I don't know where you got these words from, where you got these facts from.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you'd like to look at page 8630 in the Croatian version, 86 -- beginning at 8630, continuing to 31.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you could put 0380 on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you have page 8630, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it in front of me. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did not President Tudjman say, "What does integral Bosnia mean? Who will take us to the Drina? And besides, even if we could get to the Drina, what if we get an integral Bosnia with 2 million Serbs and 2 million Muslims what kinds of Croatia would that be? That would be even worse, the Croatian people would be even worse off than in Tito's Yugoslavia." Isn't that what he said, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what is written but I can't confirm that these are the words of the president of the Republic of Croatia, and the president of HDZ Croatia, Dr. Tudjman. If you have the recording of this, can you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'll ask you the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot keep quiet. I made a note of the page, and if I have the time, I will go back to the page that I've marked in my re-- even if this was reliable, I cannot be the judge of that, let the people who were in this meeting be the judges of that, they are the only ones who can confirm this, but the sentence taken out from the context, in this way, I do have a translation here, and presented in such a way to the witness, has nothing whatsoever to do with the text which precedes or the text which follows. If this is allowed, okay, but I don't know whether this is allowed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, your witness says that he can't confirm whether this was said or not. His memory doesn't rise to that so I don't know what you're objecting about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I waited for my witness to finish. I'm just objecting and asking whether the Prosecutor can do that in the -- in his cross-examination. I didn't dare do the same thing in my cross-examination. Because the document has to be integral, has to be in front of the witness. The witness should have read it in its integral version. I should have presented it to him. And then point to a specific question. There are 500 pages here and just two sentences are taken out and the question is, is that that? This is exactly -- this was my point. I just wanted to ask you whether this was allowed or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: If the witness were to say, Mr. Krsnik, this is out of context, give me an opportunity to read it, but this witness has consistently said that he doesn't recall, and he can't confirm or deny. If the witness -- and Mr. Krsnik, maybe we could all take lessons in a shorter style.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm concluding, I would have more I would have covered other transcripts but I promised the Chamber I would finish I just want to respond to this last comment. Mr. President, the record will show that last evening, I agreed, and I think frankly somewhat out of the ordinary, that this witness could take all the transcripts and read them all. He had them all night. He had them for some 12 or 15 hours. Now in if the Chamber wants to take the time I'm happy I will sit here with him and we can read them all together but I pointed out the sections I wanted to put to the witness. I put those to him. I do not think I took them unfairly out of context. Of course, counsel can take him to other parts of the document if he wants to. Thank you Mr. President, I'm finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I shall try to be very brief. Re-examined by Mr. Krsnik:

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have the witness see 101 and IAC-2, Exhibit 101.1 and IAC-2? These are not long documents and I will ask you, Witness, to read them, both of them, and after that, I will put my question to you. And after that, I will seek the assistance of the Chamber. Please read them very carefully, both of them. Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, no, no, please. It is important to me. It is important to me because I shall be requesting the assistance of the Chamber. Please read carefully the Croatian versions of these two documents. Please be patient. The documents are not long. Because my question will be: Are these texts absolutely identical, down to the last comma and full stop, in Croatian, that is the B/C/S version? That is why I'm asking to you read them carefully. I know that you are tired but please help us a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I do not see that these two documents have anything to do one with the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm not saying that, I'm saying identical. That is important. Is it the identical text in these two documents, please compare them passage by passage?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: 101.1 and IAC-2?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: One thing is the joint statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, I didn't ask for the joint statement?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that is what I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, then it is not your fault. 101.1 and IAC-2.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a version of the conclusions but only one. I do not have the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, we are waiting for this other one. Well, why aren't you given it? IAC-2. That is the last document in the binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I can give it from my binder. That's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know -- compare these documents, please go passage by passage.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have the documents but just give me some time so that I can compare them.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead I've read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Are these texts absolutely identical down to the last comma and full stop, the contents?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm the identity of these two texts from one sentence to the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it the same typewriter and the form?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not the same as you can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you confirm who signed one document and who -- who is indicated as the signatory on the other document?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the other documents, indicates as the Honourable Court has it has the names of Dario Kordic, Mate Boban, Yozo Maric, without signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the other document?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the other documents with the signatures of us, from the Croat Community Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And are there the signatures or are there indicated the names of Dario Kordic, Mate Boban and Yozo Maric?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this other paper on in the first one you like and this list, Your Honours, you can find that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we have -- will you please take this B/C/S versions from me today?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I'm warned to slow down and yet I'm in a hurry because I'd really like this witness to be released today, but if we are doing without haste, then, because I think this is a very important matter and we must clear it up. And I think this is really an opportunity to get to certain things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, suppose I look at the document, suppose we look at the Croatian version, it certainly appears to be an identical document. It is not an identical document in English, although, as I said to you earlier, the language is different but the content is the same. I said that to you three hours ago. What's the points you're making?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's very simple. I hold you in very high regard, I think you are a very perceptive person and that's how I see you and that's why I always listen to you but I think we have the first proof that we are dealing here with forged documents. I am not saying anything against our learned friends. Perhaps somebody else forged these documents, perhaps. But these are the same documents. These are the same documents, typed on two different typewriters in two different forms, but the same contents. On one document we have indicated a signature is Dario Kordic, Mate Boban and on the other one has attached to it a list with several signatures. That is impossible, Your Honours. The same meeting, the same date, identical text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Why is it impossible if the signatures are on a separate page? I don't understand the point you're making. I may be stupid but I'm waiting to be elucidated or educated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it will be something else. You live in an old democracy with a rule of law, with some legal order, and I'm afraid that that is at the root of our misunderstanding. It would never occur to you that somebody would dare to such a thing to a court of law in your country. So that is perhaps the problem that is perhaps the way we are talking at cross-purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and they do but make your point is because --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My point is -- [Interpretation] We have two, two same documents with identical contents, minutes of a meeting. On one of these documents, we see that is the minute taker -- we have minute taker, president and vice-president, identical document, Your Honours, of that same meeting was typed on another typewriter in a different format. These three people are not there. These three people are not there. And even though the Prosecutor had the opportunity to examine Mr. Bozo Raic and examine them about this same document, he did not show them this second document which is identical but now with a number of signatures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I only stand because of the hour. Assuming Mr. Krsnik wants to make -- well, he obviously does, we can have this argument but this witness apparently cannot shed any light on this at all so why are we doing this now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will finish the testimony of this witness -- I think you have made your point there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, no, no, no. I'm behaving very obeyingly. I'm not doing anything but I'm not sure you do not understand me. Perhaps you do not understand what is in my head what I'm trying to say because this is not the first document I've come across. I've spent my nights studying various documents that I've been given and I've come across hundreds of similar things. Irrespective of what this witness said perhaps I do not understand the Court proceedings and I apologise to Mr. Scott because I have not said anything against the gentleman in the Prosecution, because I do know who supplies them with document and where they are getting this document from, they did not go to look for it personally. It is being brought to them and I know from which centre it comes from. But now we have proof. That somebody is forging --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I ask that the witness be excused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, do you have any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more question, a misunderstanding and I wanted to clear it up. That had to do with minutes and the manner in which meetings are conducted. And the best example is the Prosecutor's Exhibit, the minutes of the Livno meeting, I do not know the number of the page. To clarify it for the Honourable Court, how minutes are taken, what happens to them, once meetings are over and so on and so forth. And that will be my last question. So please, slowly, I am sorry, I think it was not fully -- we did not clarify fully the procedure of minute taking at meetings where you were present.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said that but I can repeat it. At our meetings, we had an official person responsible for the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, was it in this case, Mrs. Andjelka Stojic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You do somewhere, only all you have to do is find it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that at the meetings of the Croat Democratic Union, Mrs. Stojic did take minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Right. What happens then to the minutes once she has taken these minutes?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minutes remained in the archive and the summary of what was said with conclusions that were adopted are drawn up and submitted at the next meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But were there also people who certified the minutes? Did you use that particular procedure?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. There were people who certified those minutes but not at all meetings. They were not present at all meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And before every meeting, is also the chair elected to conduct the meeting or to moderate the meeting? Isn't the minutes one of the items on the agenda, one of the mandatory items on the agenda indicate also who will be taking the minutes and who will be certifying the minutes?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the meeting I was present at, that was usually done because that is a rule which applies in all the civilised systems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Ask him, Mr. Krsnik, was there an agenda?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was there an agenda at every meeting?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why of course, you can't have a meeting without an agenda. Every meeting, every meeting that I attended would adopt the agenda -- would have an agenda adopted and then one worked on the basis of the agenda. For me, as a graduate in law, and for other responsible persons, that is how it should be. We are not a disorganised gang who was -- who were rounded up in the street and brought in to talk over something. So there was the agenda and all the rest, don't make me repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did the -- one of the items who -- which said who would take the minutes and the full name of that person?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of every meeting, it would be established who would take the minutes, that is record what was being said at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, must we finish today, Your Honours, this witness? I do not know whether Your Honours have questions. Perhaps we could do it tomorrow for another half hour so that we could do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... at most 15 minutes more after 7.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I'd like to ask you if we could finish it today. I'd be grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, will you please be so kind, I do not know if it is in the transcript we are talking about items on the agenda, so one. Items and the agenda and the person who will be taking minutes. The full name of that person, did have to be stated in the relevant item of the agenda?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of the meeting, meetings that I was present at, we would always adopt the agenda and also designate the person who would be responsible for the minutes. And at times we also had persons who would be certifying the minutes, but a minute taker was always designated by full name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And finally, are you ready, are you ready to help -- well, now I say the defence, when you return home, and if I get a break or at some other point in time, would you be ready that we together, at least with regard to these documents that you said whilst you held those offices and that you said that you were responsible for them, that is the House of Representatives, would you agree that we try to locate them together and then I would notify the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said and I stand by what I said, that we can do it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and, God willing, I will be leaving tomorrow in the direction of Neum and Mostar, and I am at your disposal about the things that I have said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions. Thank you very much Mr. Bender, for coming here and thank you very much for helping the Honourable Court to gain as good an insight as possible into the subjects that we are discussing here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IVAN BENDER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to thank the Honourable Court for their fair and correct treatment. I -- it will make me very happy if my presentation has helped to establish the truth and it will contribute towards a fair judgement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, on behalf of the bench, I would like to thank you very much for coming here to give your testimony. We appreciate it very much. All of us wish you a good trip back home. The usher will show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we are five minutes past the time. I have to apologise, make our apologies to the interpreters and the court reporter for the delay. So we will resume tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 7.05 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 24th day of May, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25
